text: The book notes that the presentist and block-universe (eternalist) interpretations “give identical physical predictions.” What methodological conclusion does it draw?
choices: Presentism has been experimentally refuted, leaving eternalism as the only scientifically respectable option
The dispute is merely verbal and dissolves once the key terms are carefully defined
The metaphysics of time is underdetermined by physics, so settling which times are real requires distinctively philosophical work
Because physics cannot decide between them, the question of what is real is meaningless
explanation: The book treats this as a structural case of underdetermination: identical predictions leave 'which times are real?' open, so philosophy must go beyond physics. It explicitly denies that physics refutes presentism (the predictions are identical) and rejects the positivist 'physics-imperialist' claim that an empirically undecidable question is thereby meaningless.
